Spike the fixed product-meaning-free CounterSpike oracle under src/hermes_pipeline/domain/ with a frozen semantic: initial state is strictly (value=0, revision=0); from any (value=v, revision=r), accepting Increment(delta=1) transitions the state strictly to (v+1, r+1) and produces the unique domain Event CounterIncremented whose payload exactly contains the new value and the new revision; command identity is carried by the existing Controller envelope; any delta different from 1 returns the typed INVALID_DELTA result, leaves the state completely unchanged, and produces no domain Event; expected-revision conflict handling remains the Controller persistence layer's responsibility, not the domain's; the evaluator has no I/O, clock, identity, randomness, or framework dependency and is a candidate for retention, clearly marked non-public

Define a typed persistence port private to the Controller: controller depends only on that port and domain values and never imports SQLAlchemy, LangGraph, Alembic, filesystem, or concrete persistence Adapter code, and never executes SQL or filesystem operations itself; the port has a deterministic in-memory test Adapter and one SQLite spike Adapter that may use SQLAlchemy Core

Retain ControllerCommandPort.submit(command: ControllerCommand) -> CommandReceipt as the accepted external Interface and the only Interface the Stage Executor may call; it uses the existing CommandReceipt status/error model: domain INVALID_DELTA projects to REJECTED/VALIDATION_ERROR with fixed message invalid delta; same-ID/different-payload and expected-revision conflicts project to CONFLICT/CONFLICT with respectively fixed messages command identity conflict and expected revision conflict; persistence failures including SQLITE_FULL project to an in-memory, non-durable REJECTED/INTERNAL_ERROR receipt with fixed message persistence unavailable and retryable=true; no durable receipt record or partial records are written on that path, and raw sqlite3, SQLAlchemy, or driver exceptions never cross the Interface; the Stage Executor and LangGraph spike graph are forbidden to import the private persistence port, any persistence Adapter, SQLAlchemy, or database files, enforced by positive and negative import-boundary tests

Prove one atomic SQLite Controller transaction writes Inbox, Event, projection, Outbox, and receipt records all-or-none using an explicit SQLite driver transaction mode (for example SQLAlchemy connect_args autocommit=False or an explicit BEGIN event hook); the legacy sqlite3 default transaction control is never relied on and the chosen mode is documented and tested

Prove duplicate command delivery, same-command-id different-payload conflict, and expected-revision conflict: a repeated identical command returns the original receipt and appends exactly one Event; the private spike must classify the former as COMMAND_ID_CONFLICT, while the Stage-visible receipt is CONFLICT/CONFLICT with fixed message command identity conflict; expected-revision mismatch uses CONFLICT/CONFLICT with fixed message expected revision conflict; neither rejection appends an Event or Outbox row

Separate transaction-failure and process-crash evidence: AC-03 injects an exception before and after each of the five logical writes inside the transaction and proves the whole transaction rolls back; AC-05 crashes a real subprocess only at the true durable boundaries (pre-commit and post-commit of the five-record transaction) and restarts a fresh process from the same database and WAL; ordinary exception injection is never presented as crash evidence

Translate every driver failure at the Interface boundary: ControllerCommandPort.submit returns the schema-compatible, non-durable CommandReceipt specified above; backup and migration test-helper Interfaces return bounded non-serialized typed results; no traceback, raw SQL, absolute path, database content, or raw exception text crosses any Interface; output is bounded; the spike does not change committed Schemas or the accepted Controller signature and does not turn spike errors into a product public API
Prove projection rebuild: a projection rebuilt from the authoritative Event Log with Event hash-chain verification equals the live projection for the same Event set

Prove online backup and restore through the Python sqlite3.Connection.backup API while a reader or writer is active, then validate the restored copy with PRAGMA integrity_check and PRAGMA foreign_key_check; the backup API and policy reject the raw-copy path before any I/O, and a guard or mock proves the implementation only ever calls sqlite3.Connection.backup(); no test asserts that a raw copy necessarily corrupts the database; the backup helper returns bounded typed results and never exposes raw driver exceptions

Record sqlite3.sqlite_version on both required platforms and apply the exact SQLite WAL-reset repair-version predicate: at least 3.51.3, or at least 3.50.7 and below 3.51.0, or at least 3.44.6 and below 3.45.0, with committed accept and reject version vectors; a linked library failing the predicate on either platform stops the Slice with a Contract Change Request before any spike persistence conclusion is claimed

Run the fixed reproducible single-writer workload envelope: 1,000 accepted commands, 4 producers, one writer, queue capacity 32, command and event payloads each no larger than 1 KiB, p95 acknowledged latency no greater than 2 seconds, busy count equal to 0, WAL high-water no greater than 16 MiB, and checkpoint, online backup, and fresh-process recovery each no greater than 5 seconds; the report records a fixed redacted runner profile (OS family, architecture, CI runner label, Python version, and sqlite3.sqlite_version) plus selected PRAGMAs and queue high-water; hostname, username, absolute paths, environment variable values, tokens, raw exception text, and database content are forbidden from test output and the Execution Report, with a verifiable redaction assertion that injects fake sensitive values and proves the reporter does not leak them; a deterministic SQLITE_FULL injection returns the specified non-durable REJECTED/INTERNAL_ERROR receipt, writes no durable receipt record or partial records, is restart-safe, and never exhausts real disk; an exceeded limit or unrecordable evidence triggers the already-planned replacement-ADR path (Phase risk R-03)

risks.description: The linked SQLite library on a required platform is below the exact WAL-reset repair-version predicate (at least 3.51.3, or at least 3.50.7 and below 3.51.0, or at least 3.44.6 and below 3.45.0), exposing concurrent WAL write or checkpoint corruption.
risks.mitigation: Record sqlite3.sqlite_version on both platforms, gate it against the exact predicate with committed accept and reject version vectors, and stop with a Contract Change Request before claiming any spike persistence conclusion when a platform fails.
risks.trigger: Either platform links an SQLite library failing the predicate or a version vector disagrees.

risks.description: The fixed single-writer workload envelope (1,000 accepted commands, 4 producers, queue capacity 32, 1 KiB payloads, p95 within 2 seconds, busy 0, WAL high-water within 16 MiB, checkpoint, backup, and recovery within 5 seconds each) is exceeded, or a metric cannot be recorded.
risks.mitigation: Declare the fixed envelope as the acceptance boundary, measure every metric including queue high-water, run the deterministic SQLITE_FULL injection on a bounded fixture mapping to the specified non-durable REJECTED/INTERNAL_ERROR CommandReceipt, and raise the already-planned replacement-ADR decision instead of claiming SQLite scales indefinitely.
risks.trigger: A declared envelope limit is exceeded or the evidence cannot be recorded.

risks.description: The five-record Controller write is not atomic, an acknowledged command is lost after restart, a replay duplicates an Event, or a driver failure crosses the Interface as a raw exception.
risks.mitigation: Inject exceptions before and after every logical write for rollback evidence, translate every driver failure into the specified safe non-durable CommandReceipt or a bounded private helper result, crash a real subprocess only at the pre-commit and post-commit durable boundaries, restart from the same database and WAL in fresh processes, and assert all-or-none commits, exactly one Event per command, and the original receipt on replay.
risks.trigger: Any subset of the five records commits alone, an acknowledged command is lost, a replay appends a second Event, or a raw driver exception or sensitive payload crosses the Interface.

risks.description: LangGraph replay or checkpoint loss duplicates a Controller transition, the Stage Executor imports a forbidden persistence surface, or the checkpoint database gains authority over Controller state.
risks.mitigation: Route all Stage Executor business effects through ControllerCommandPort.submit with a stable Controller command ID, prove exactly one Event and one stable receipt including under sync-durability checkpoint loss, enforce positive and negative Stage Executor import-boundary tests, and prove the checkpoint database cannot write Controller tables or advance state.
risks.trigger: A replay appends a second Event, a receipt is unstable, a Stage Executor import violates the boundary, or the checkpoint database advances Controller state.

risks.description: The spike silently relies on the legacy sqlite3 default transaction control, promises rollback-atomic Alembic migration batches, or presents exception injection as process-crash evidence.
risks.mitigation: Select and test one explicit SQLite driver transaction mode, record Alembic begin_transaction as a logical transaction with upgrade and rollback evidence plus injected-failure recovery through verified backup, and keep AC-03 exception injection separate from AC-05 real subprocess crashes.
risks.trigger: Legacy transaction control is relied on, whole-migration atomicity is promised, or exception injection is presented as crash evidence.

risks.description: The transitive dependency graph, including sqlite-vec, does not resolve or execute reproducibly on Windows and Linux, or a spike package leaks into the runtime path.
risks.mitigation: Freeze the complete resolution in uv.lock with sqlite-vec wheel admission evidence, run the complete offline canonical command set on both platforms, and enforce an import-boundary regression for the plugin entry, --version, and the normal runtime path.
risks.trigger: A platform cannot resolve or execute the frozen graph, an offline canonical command fails, or a spike package is imported from the runtime path.

risks.description: Spike code is treated as production foundation without a recorded disposition, silently constraining Slice 00-07 or later design.
risks.mitigation: Mark every spike component experimental with an explicit retain-or-delete record; retain only the CounterSpike domain evaluator as a non-public candidate unless Slice 00-07 explicitly adopts the rest.
risks.trigger: A spike component is presented as production foundation without a disposition or 00-07 adoption.

risks.description: The workload reporter or any Interface leaks hostname, username, absolute paths, environment values, tokens, raw exception text, or database content into test output or the Execution Report.
risks.mitigation: Restrict the runner profile to the fixed redacted fields (OS family, architecture, CI runner label, Python version, and sqlite3.sqlite_version), forbid all other fields, and prove with a redaction assertion using injected fake sensitive values that the reporter does not leak; typed failures carry sensitive-free error codes only.
risks.trigger: A forbidden field or sensitive value appears in test output or the Execution Report.

stop_conditions: A required platform links an SQLite library failing the exact predicate (at least 3.51.3, or at least 3.50.7 and below 3.51.0, or at least 3.44.6 and below 3.45.0), or a committed version vector disagrees; stop and submit a Contract Change Request before claiming any spike persistence conclusion

Controller code must import SQLAlchemy, LangGraph, Alembic, filesystem, or a concrete persistence Adapter, must execute SQL or filesystem operations itself, or the Stage-facing ControllerCommandPort signature differs from submit(ControllerCommand) -> CommandReceipt

The Stage Executor or LangGraph graph code must import the private persistence port, a persistence Adapter, SQLAlchemy, or database files, or must reach business state outside ControllerCommandPort.submit
Inbox, Event, projection, Outbox, and receipt cannot commit atomically; an acknowledged command is lost; or a replay appends a second Event

A raw sqlite3, SQLAlchemy, or driver exception, raw SQL, an absolute path, database content, or raw exception text must cross ControllerCommandPort.submit or the backup and migration test-helper Interfaces
A cross-database transaction between the Controller database and the checkpoint database becomes necessary
The checkpoint database gains any authority to advance Controller state
A spike dependency must enter the runtime path, [project].dependencies must change, or the Hermes plugin entry, --version, or the normal runtime path must import a spike package
A declared workload envelope limit is exceeded or the evidence cannot be recorded; raise the replacement-ADR decision

The deterministic SQLITE_FULL injection cannot be produced without exhausting real disk, does not map to the specified non-durable REJECTED/INTERNAL_ERROR CommandReceipt, or leaves partial records or a durable receipt record

Rollback-atomic Alembic migration batches must be promised, the legacy sqlite3 default transaction control must be relied on, or a migration failure cannot be recovered through verified backup and recovery
Exception injection must be presented as process-crash evidence, or a raw-copy path must perform file I/O before the API or policy rejects it
